svg.aria-label: The m-l-k root carried into Greek letters, translated into Greek words, and identified with a Greek god
svg.text: מלך crossed into Greek three times: carried letter for letter, swapped for a Greek word, and set beside a Greek god on the same stone.
Joseph Yahuda argued in Hebrew Is Greek (1982) that the two languages are one. These are the artefacts he would have put first.
Every line below is a Septuagint spelling, a translator’s substitution, or a bilingual inscription — each one checkable.

svg.text: The root is still legible in Greek. And Greek has no aleph, so the aleph words and the king words fall together the moment they cross.

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif
'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: The form the world knows is the Greek one. English never met the Hebrew.

'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: Carried into Hebrews in its Greek dress and never changed back.

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif
'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: The aleph is simply gone — Greek has no letter for it, so in Greek this is μ-λ-χ, the
same three signs as Μελχισέδεκ. Nor is the convergence only Greek: the Punic corpus
writes MLKT where MLʾKT is meant, Palmyrene has mlkbl, “Messenger of Baal”, and Arabic
keeps malik the king beside malak the angel in one set of letters.

svg.text: Read as mlk-qrt, King of the City — a reconstruction, and the usual one. Greek writers

svg.text: THE WORD CARRIED, THE LETTERS DID NOT
A Greek word was put in the place of the Hebrew one, and English took the Greek.

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif
'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: Both words mean exactly the same thing, and the Greek one has no settled parentage of
its own: the Indo-European comparison is abandoned, Beekes sets it beside ἄγγαρος out
of the East, and Gussetius derived it from הִגִּיד, "he announced".

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif
'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: The heaviest substitution in the book. Teaching became statute, and most of what has
been argued about since follows from it.

svg.text: THE SAME FOUR LETTERS, READ TWO WAYS — BY PEOPLE WHO HAD NO VOWEL POINTS
Not our reconstruction. The Greek translators’ own split, book against book.

svg.text: “to MOLOCH, in the fire” — carried over as a name
One written word, two decisions, taken by the same tradition in different books and five to eight centuries before anyone wrote a vowel.
And the field was open in Hebrew too. At 2 Samuel 11:1 the text writes הַמַּלְאָכִים, “the MESSENGERS”, at the moment it means “when KINGS go out to
Rendsburg calls that visual word play — it exists, he writes, “solely from the written form of the text”. The reader saw both and knew which was

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: THE SAME GOD, ON ONE STONE
The Cippi of Melqart — the bilingual that let Europe read Phoenician.

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: l'dnn lmlqrt b'l ṣr — “to our lord Melqart, Baal of Tyre”

text.font-family: 'Noto Sans Hebrew','Noto Serif Hebrew','SBL Hebrew','Times New Roman','DejaVu Sans','FreeSerif',serif

svg.text: Two marble cippi from Tas-Silġ in Malta, 2nd century BC. One dedication, cut twice: Punic on the base, Greek above it.
The same two brothers, the same god, and on the Greek face the god of the m-l-k root is simply called Herakles.
In 1758 Jean-Jacques Barthélemy read the Punic off the Greek and recovered 18 of the 22 Phoenician letters from it.
So the root is not merely comparable to Greek. It is on the object by which Europe learned to read Phoenician at all.
One cippus is in the Louvre; its twin is in Valletta.
The vowels were a choice made in Hebrew. This was the choice made in Greek — and it is the Greek choice that most of the world received.
